title: ingress-adaptive-fallback-and-soft-deny-safeguard
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Adds an ingress-level adaptive fallback and soft-deny policy to improve SLO preservation during regional egress degradation. Opt-in via config; no public API changes.
description: Context and motivation: Shortly after a regional egress incident we observed a class of customer errors where upstream egress timeouts caused cascading retries and overloaded the regional ingress layer, resulting in rapid SLO erosion for 95p latency and elevated error budgets. This PR introduces an ingress-level adaptive fallback and 'soft-deny' policy that (1) enforces SLO-aware admission by short-circuiting expensive slowpath work, (2) triggers a lightweight circuit-breaker for downstream egress pressure, and (3) performs a controlled load-shedding step before routing to regional failover. Design summary: - Introduce an ingress admission gate that calculates a rolling SLO headroom score (based on per-route 95/99 latency and error rate) and attaches a decision token to the request context. - When headroom < threshold, the gate applies soft-deny strategies ordered by policy: early prefix-cache short-circuit, reduced batching allowance, and finally a graceful 429 with structured retry-after metadata. - A local circuit-breaker watches egress latency/error signals and engages an ingress backpressure mode that converts low-priority requests to soft-deny earlier, and marks high-priority routes for immediate failover. - A telemetry shim captures pre/post decision trace markers (ingress.decide, ingress.softdeny, ingress.egress-cb) to correlate effects with SLO metrics. Key behaviors: - Soft-deny returns structured JSON with a reason code and suggested client retry window (helps SDKs back off deterministically). - Configurable per-tenant and per-route weights so large enterprise tenants can be exempted or have different thresholds. - Defaults conservative: feature off for main until rollout steps complete. Commits summary: - add: services/ingress/decision_gate.go (rolling headroom scorer + config) - add: services/ingress/soft_deny_handler.go (soft deny responses and backoff guidance) - update: runtime/request_router.go (attach decision tokens and routing hooks) - update: controlplane/config_types.go (opt-in flags and per-tenant overrides) - add: telemetry/markers/ingress_tags.proto - add: unit and integration tests for gate behaviors (ingress_gate_test.go, soft_deny_integration_test.go) Files changed (high level): - services/ingress/* (core logic) - runtime/* (hook points) - controlplane/* (config) - telemetry/* (markers) - docs/ops/ingress-fallback.md (operator runbook) Testing and CI: - Unit tests added for headroom scoring and soft-deny response semantics. - Integration test simulating egress latency spikes and verifying soft-deny ordering. - CI initially reported an intermittent integration flake on the simulated egress harness; re-ran pipeline and all checks passed. Rollout plan: 1) Merge to main with feature flag disabled by default. 2) Canary on a single low-traffic region with per-route logging enabled for 48h. 3) Enable conservative thresholds (headroom 0.15) and monitor 95/99 latency, error budget burn, and ingress.decide metrics. 4) If stable, widen to additional regions with staggered ramp. 5) Provide an emergency toggle to force-disable soft-deny across all regions. Observability and alerts: - New SLO-derived metric ingress/headroom_score. - Alert: headroom_score < 0.05 for 10m triggers runbook. - Dashboards updated in ops/dashboards/ingress-fallback.json. Backwards compatibility & safety: - No changes to public APIs or SDK surface. - Default behavior is a no-op unless enabled via config or per-tenant flags. - Soft-deny uses structured responses so SDKs can make informed retry decisions. Risk and mitigations: - Risk: poorly calibrated thresholds could increase client-visible 429s. Mitigation: conservative defaults, canary rollout, and per-tenant overrides. - Risk: false positives if telemetry noise spikes headroom low. Mitigation: 1min rolling windows and a short cooldown for circuit transitions. Related work: follows earlier regional fallback projects but focuses earlier in the request path (ingress) to avoid queuing amplification. References: Linear ENG-6721, incident SUP-345. Checklist: - [x] design doc linked - [x] unit tests added - [x] integration tests added - [x] ops runbook and dashboard updates - [x] feature-flag gated - [x] reviewers sign-off - [x] canary plan documented Review conversation (high-level): see review_comments field for excerpts.
